source.author: verg
source.text: Quin etiam bis tum medios invaserat hostis, bis confusa fuga per muros agmina vertit; sed manus e castris propere coit omnis in unum, nec contra vires audet Saturnia Iuno sufficere, aëriam caelo nam Iuppiter Irim demisit germanae haud mollia iussa ferentem, ni Turnus cedat Teucrorum moenibus altis.
source.text_original: Quin etiam bis tum medios invaserat hostis, / bis confusa fuga per muros agmina vertit; / sed manus e castris propere coit omnis in unum, / nec contra vires audet Saturnia Iuno / sufficere, aëriam caelo nam Iuppiter Irim / demisit germanae haud mollia iussa ferentem, / ni Turnus cedat Teucrorum moenibus altis.
source.text_english: Indeed, even then the enemy had twice broken into the middle of the city, twice had scattered the confused ranks in flight through the walls; but all the force from the camp quickly gathered together into one body, and Saturnian Juno does not dare to oppose strength with strength, for Jupiter from heaven had sent down airy Iris, bearing to his sister stern orders: that Turnus must yield to the high walls of the Teucrians.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: nunc aerii plantaria vellet Perseos aut curru saevos frenasse dracones ardet, ut ignaras Cereris qui vomere terras imbuit et flava quercum damnavit arista.
reuse.text_original: nunc aerii plantaria vellet / Perseos aut curru saevos frenasse dracones / ardet, ut ignaras Cereris qui vomere terras / imbuit et flava quercum damnavit arista.
reuse.text_english: Now he burns to wish for the seedlings of airy Perseus or to have tamed the savage dragons with a chariot, like the man who first seasoned the lands ignorant of Ceres with the plowshare and condemned the oak with golden grain.
